To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hybrid beams exhibit creep deflections that increase over time, and the creep deflections of the GFRP profile are significantly higher than those of the hybrid beams.
the creep deflections on hybrid beams are significant and that the failure mechanism is related to the degradation of bond between the GFRP profile and the concrete slab.
the hybrid beams are able to withstand sustained loads, however, the degradation of bond strength is the main factor that leads to premature failures.

the experimental and numerical investigation of the long term performance of a hybrid beam made of a GFRG profile bonded to an RC slab, under sustained loads.
the development of a reliable design method for GFRP concrete composite structures, based on the results obtained in the present work and in our previous investigations.
the long term behaviour and durability of GFRP reinforced concrete hybrid structures.

the proposed numerical approach can accurately predict the creep and shrinkage behaviour of hybrid beams.
the proposed hybrid beam system, with its high initial stiffness, can be used for the construction of lightweight structures with high durability and low environmental impact.
the hybrid beam, which was designed to resist the short term loads, failed prematurely because the long term behaviour could not be predicted by the designer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed numerical models are able to predict the long term behaviour and failure of the hybrid structures with a good level of accuracy.
the long term behaviour is a function of the creep behaviour of the materials and of the degradation of the adhesive joint.

the hybrid beams are able to sustain a significant amount of sustained loads, but the bond strength between the GFRP and the concrete is the critical factor in determining the long term performance of the structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a pultruded GFRP profile bonded to a reinforced concrete beam, in order to increase the flexural capacity, may not be an efficient strategy for the design of long term structures, due to the rapid degradation of the bond strength.
the long term behaviour can be predicted using finite element analysis and that it is necessary to account for creep effects when predicting the long term performance of hybrid beams.
